s1.syndrome_frame: bilateral breast lumps with rapid onset and varying characteristics, associated with lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
left breast lump fixed to the chest wall with irregular spiculated mass on MRI
right breast lump firm and mobile with well-defined lesion on MRI
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
previously regular menstrual cycles
left breast lump 4 × 4 cm, hard, fixed to chest wall
right breast lump 1 × 1 cm, firm, mobile
MRI showed irregular spiculated mass in left breast
MRI showed well-defined lesion in right breast
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI
ultrasound and bone scan negative for metastases
fine-needle aspiration cytology of left breast lump showed malignant cells
FNAC of left axillary lymph node showed malignant cells
FNAC of right breast lump showed hyperchromatic cells with prominent nucleoli
core-needle biopsy of left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma
estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

shortlist.label: Bilateral invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: malignant cells in both breasts and lymph node metastasis

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: right breast lump characteristics and benign cytology

shortlist.label: Breast lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy and rapid onset

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rapid growth and varying characteristics of breast lumps

raw.rationale: The presence of malignant cells in both breasts, as shown by fine-needle aspiration cytology, and the confirmation of infiltrative duct cell carcinoma in the left breast by core-needle biopsy, support this diagnosis. Additionally, the MRI findings of a spiculated mass in the left breast and a well-defined lesion in the right breast, along with bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, are consistent with bilateral invasive ductal carcinoma.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic inflammatory breast cancer symptoms such as skin changes, redness, or warmth.

rejected.label: Fibroadenoma
rejected.why: While the right breast lump was initially suspected to be a fibroadenoma, the presence of hyperchromatic cells with prominent nucleoli and scattered pleomorphic cells in the FNAC suggests a more complex diagnosis.

rejected.label: Breast lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of lymphoma, such as a significant increase in lymphoid cells, to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: The cytologic and biopsy findings do not support the diagnosis of a phyllodes tumor, which typically has a distinct histological appearance.
